title: Why make the jump to Enterprise Architect
oneliner: A solution architect goes deep on one area; an enterprise architect goes wide across business, data, application, and technology - and governs all of it.
says: He makes the case that solution and cloud architects should consider the enterprise architect path. As a solution architect you focus on one area - infrastructure, platform, or application solutioning. As an enterprise architect your view expands to business architecture, data architecture, technology architecture, application architecture, plus implementation governance and operational excellence. Getting there needs the right project opportunity in your organization, and certifications like TOGAF help.
explained: This is the classic depth-versus-breadth fork in an architecture career. The solution architect's power is credibility in the details: you can design the actual system. The enterprise architect's power is coherence across the whole estate: every team's decisions add up to one direction, standards get enforced, and technology spend traces to business strategy.

His practical point deserves emphasis: you cannot study your way into this role. You need a project where the wide view is actually yours - and those go to people who have already shown they can hold more than their own lane. The certification (he mentions TOGAF) gives you the shared vocabulary of business/data/application/technology architecture, but the opportunity has to be earned inside your organization first.
takeaway: If you want the EA path, start acting wide before the title arrives - volunteer for cross-cutting work, then let the certification formalize it.
